body:
Theme Detectives: 1. Ravi's snow walls keep collapsing because the snow is too fluffy, and he will not accept help. 2. He waves Mina away and says, "You'll just knock it down." 3. He looks at the pile of mush that used to be his wall and realizes his way is not working. 4. At the end he shares the credit and calls it "Our fort," and he grins at his sister. 5. Example themes: Working together can make a hard job possible. Accepting help is not the same as failing. 6. Any detail that shows the change works; strongest: Mina's packed blocks make the fort possible, or "Our fort."
The Theme of "The Kite That Would Not Fly": Strong themes: Do not give up when something fails the first time; a mistake can be fixed; the people who love us can help us solve problems. Strong details: the kite crashes three times; Lila nearly throws it away; her grandfather says a broken kite and an unfinished kite are not the same; she adds ribbons from her old dress; the kite flies higher than any other.
Theme Check: Strong themes: You do not have to be the loudest to be important; every part of a team matters; being steady can matter more than being noticed. Noor changes from wanting attention (she picks the biggest drum and plays the loudest) to understanding her role (she keeps a steady beat, the band leans on it, and she is proud though nobody claps). Strong details: "the drum is not a race"; her sticks "hovered above it like birds"; the band falls apart; "Not loud. Just steady."; "every note in the room had been standing on her beat."
Scoring tip: a response that names a topic ("drums," "kites") is Beginning on the theme criterion even if the details are strong; score the evidence criterion on its own.
title: Answer key: Finding the Theme
